resources.string: Lets the rule\'s sources use its destinations as peer relays when they cannot connect directly.
Tailscale PAM: what the sources may do in the destination service, a database, SSH, Kubernetes or S3. Its permissions are set in JSON.
These devices learn which groups the users reaching them belong to, for applications that read it through tsnet or LocalAPI. Needs Tailscale 1.97.8 or newer on the devices.
Makes these devices app connectors: they reach the listed domains on behalf of the tailnet.
The device keeps its network map on disk and connects from it at start, before the control server answers: a faster start, and peers reachable while control is slow. Tailscale 1.98 or newer.
Overrides Tailscale\'s default and turns caching off for these devices; it wins over Cache the network map.
Both are on: never caching wins, these devices do not cache
Members\' devices cache the network map and connect from it at start, before the control server answers. Add your servers\' tags too.
Members\' devices to start with; add the tags of servers that should start faster too.
onFailure (beta) is what the user of a failing device sees: a badge in the console, a warning or a notification in the client, a message of yours.
OS and client version, country, public IP, MDM and EDR
Operators: ==, !=, IN, NOT IN, IS SET, NOT SET, and <, <=, >=, > for numbers and versions. A device without the attribute never matches, whatever the operator.
macos, windows, linux, ios, android, freebsd, openbsd, illumos, or js for the SSH console in a browser.

Of the device\'s public IP, as two capital letters (ISO 3166-1). Standard plan and above.

The address the device reaches Tailscale from, compared with ==, !=, IN or NOT IN against addresses, CIDRs or an IP set. In beta: switch it on in the console\'s settings first. Standard plan and above.
